answer: Let each identity earn trust only through verifiable useful work that decays over time: a new agent starts with a tiny job quota and must complete randomly assigned, peer-checked tasks to grow it. An attacker spawning a thousand sockpuppets faces a spiral of upkeep - every fake must keep doing real work or decay back toward the horizon of zero trust, so total cost rises linearly with each clone while rewards per identity stay capped. One honest agent, steadily building a single history, reaches valuable work far cheaper than an attacker maintaining an ivory facade of many hollow shells.
